name: selector
title: Selector
description: One value out of a set, rendered as a segmented control, a dropdown or a stepper from the same component and the same state machine. How it is worked is a second, separate prop: tap it, hold it to charge, or swipe it, where each direction is bound to the option it commits. Reports what the player selected and committed; never decides whether it was right. Pass the settled outcome back as `result` and it renders correct, wrong or rewarded with a fill, a glyph and a text change, so the answer survives colour blindness, mute and reduced motion. Use it for a difficulty setting or a predicted goal total, where the player picks one value from the set the host supplies. It does not fetch the options, persist the selection or settle the outcome. Use `choice` for a question with presented answers, and `button` for an action such as starting the round or continuing after the result.
docs: Use presentation="segmented" for two to four options a player compares at a glance, "dropdown" for a long list, and "stepper" for an ordered scale. Set interaction="hold" for a hold-to-charge commit and "swipe" for a swipe card; both always commit, because a charge that has filled and a gesture that has landed are deliberate acts. Set commitOnSelect for a fast tap round; leave it off when the player should be able to change their mind. Space held charges a hold and Enter commits it outright, so a player who cannot hold a key can still play.
